title: WHY: 2025 Global Forum Identity
subtitle: Branding · Event Design
desc: A visual identity for WHY: 2025, a global forum on design leadership. The system had to work across a stage backdrop, delegate materials, and a live broadcast, so it was built around a single adaptable mark rather than a fixed lockup.
background: WHY: 2025 needed an identity that could survive very different environments in the same week — a stage backdrop seen from the back of a hall, delegate badges and printed materials seen up close, and a live broadcast compressed into a small frame.
insight: Rather than lock the forum to one static composition, the system was built around a single adaptable mark that rescales and recomposes for each surface, keeping WHY: 2025 recognizable everywhere without ever looking like three different events.

title: Hongik IDAS Program Rebrand
subtitle: Identity Design · Education
desc: A rebrand for a graduate design-management program, translating an academic mission into a mark and system that reads clearly on diplomas, signage, and admissions materials alike.
background: A graduate design-management program needed its identity to speak to two audiences at once: prospective students weighing a serious academic choice, and the institution's own diplomas, signage, and formal materials that outlive any single marketing cycle.
insight: The rebrand translates the program's academic mission into a mark restrained enough to sit comfortably on a diploma, yet distinctive enough to stand out in an admissions brochure — one system doing double duty across the program's most formal and most persuasive materials.

title: CLAB Research Archive Website
subtitle: UX Design · Digital
desc: An interface for browsing years of design-leadership research, prioritizing fast scanning over decoration so returning researchers can find a paper or case study in a few clicks.
background: Years of design-leadership research had accumulated with no single way to browse it, so returning researchers were re-finding papers through search engines instead of the archive itself.
insight: The interface was built around fast scanning rather than decoration — clear filters, consistent card layouts, and minimal visual noise — so a returning researcher can locate a specific paper or case study in a few clicks instead of a few minutes.

title: Human Factors in Leadership Visual System
subtitle: Design Research · Branding
desc: A visual system for CLAB's seminar series on human factors in leadership, built to travel between printed programs, a lecture hall backdrop, and a set of social recap graphics.
background: CLAB's seminar series on human factors in leadership runs across a printed program, a lecture hall backdrop, and a set of social recap graphics produced right after each session, so the visual system had to travel light and assemble quickly between formats.
insight: A shared set of typographic and graphic rules — rather than a single fixed layout — lets the same identity scale from a printed program to a projected backdrop to a same-day social recap without a new design pass for every format.

title: GDLA Annual Report 2025
subtitle: Editorial · Typography
desc: An editorial system for the association's annual report, using a single typographic voice to hold a year of statistics, essays, and project summaries together without a photograph in sight.
background: A year of statistics, essays, and project summaries needed to read as one coherent report rather than a bound stack of separate documents, without leaning on photography to carry the visual interest.
insight: The editorial system uses a single typographic voice — considered scale, spacing, and hierarchy — to hold numbers, narrative, and project recaps together, proving a report can feel visually rich through typography alone.
